laptop.lenovo-thinkpad-t16-gen-3: A 16-inch business laptop with a pleasant keyboard and user-upgradeable RAM. The catch: the Core Ultra chips are modest on performance, and the fan gets noticeable under load.
laptop.alienware-16-area-51: A heavy 16-inch desktop replacement with strong RTX 5080 performance, an optional Cherry MX keyboard reviewers like and three M.2 slots. The catch: short battery life and a weight over 7 lbs.
laptop.apple-macbook-air-13-m5: A fast, silent, fanless ultraportable with all-day battery and a strong keyboard, which reviewers say suits most people. The catch: the display is still 60Hz.
laptop.apple-macbook-neo: A budget aluminum MacBook with quick everyday performance, good battery life and a strong keyboard and trackpad. The catch: only 8GB of RAM, plus no keyboard backlight.
laptop.dell-xps-14-da14260: A thin aluminum 14-inch laptop with a well-liked OLED option and long battery life, especially on the IPS versions. The catch: the price is high, and ports are limited to USB-C.
laptop.dell-xps-16-da16260: A slim, light 16-inch aluminum laptop with a sharp tandem OLED screen and integrated graphics that suit office and creative work. The catch: only three USB-C ports, with no HDMI or SD card reader.
laptop.microsoft-surface-laptop-13-1st-edition: A 13-inch Windows on Arm laptop with long battery life and quiet running on the Snapdragon X Plus version. The catch: a 60Hz screen, and several reviewers favor the 13.8-inch Surface Laptop.
laptop.samsung-galaxy-book5-pro: A light aluminum 14-inch laptop with a vivid 120Hz AMOLED screen and smooth Galaxy phone integration. The catch: shallow keyboard travel, and several reviewers also found the speakers weak.
laptop.acer-chromebook-plus-spin-514-cp514-5hn: A fast Chromebook convertible with a Kompanio Ultra 910 chip and battery that gets through a full workday. The catch: it is expensive and some reviewers found the speakers muddy or harsh.
laptop.apple-macbook-pro-14-m6: A faster 14-inch MacBook Pro with the M6 chip and very long battery life. The catch: it is a modest update, with the display carried over from last year.
laptop.dell-xps-13-dx13260: A light aluminum 13-inch laptop with very long battery life and loud, clear speakers. The catch: the Core 5 320 chip is modest and graphics are weak, so it suits basic work only.
laptop.framework-laptop-13-pro: A repairable 13-inch laptop with a sturdier aluminum chassis, bright display and long battery life. The catch: the price is very high and the CPU runs warm without matching rival speed.
laptop.gigabyte-aorus-master-16-am6h: A powerful 240Hz OLED gaming laptop with strong RTX 5080 gaming performance. The catch: fans are very loud, battery life is short and the build feels plasticky.
laptop.hp-elitebook-ultra-g1i: A 14-inch business laptop with a Core Ultra 7 chip, a great OLED screen and long battery life. The catch: memory is soldered and multi-core speed trails AMD rivals.
laptop.hp-elitebook-x-g1a: A sturdy 14-inch business laptop with a fast Ryzen AI chip and a comfortable keyboard. The catch: it is heavy and pricey, and battery life lags some rivals.
laptop.hp-omen-max-16-2025: A powerful RTX 5090 gaming laptop with one of the best OLED screens reviewers have tested. The catch: battery life is short, fans are loud and the CPU runs hot.
laptop.hp-omnibook-5-14-14-he0000: A light Snapdragon laptop with an OLED screen, a good keyboard and very long battery life. The catch: graphics are weak, Arm app compatibility is limited and the 300 nit panel is prone to glare.
laptop.hp-omnibook-7-14-14-fr0000: A solid aluminum 14-inch laptop that is quick in its Core Ultra 7 255H version and quiet in light use. The catch: it weighs more than HP states and keyboard travel is shallow.
laptop.hp-zbook-ultra-g1a: A compact 14-inch workstation with the Ryzen AI Max chip, strong CPU speed and an excellent OLED screen. The catch: battery life is short for the power and memory is soldered.
laptop.lenovo-thinkpad-t14s-gen-7: A light ThinkPad at roughly 1.07 kg with a comfortable keyboard and a bright OLED screen. The catch: graphics are integrated only and memory is soldered, so capacity must be picked at purchase.
laptop.lenovo-yoga-slim-7x-gen-11: A light Snapdragon X2 Elite laptop with fast Arm-native CPU speed, very long battery life and a vivid OLED. The catch: graphics are weak, x86 apps slow under emulation and ports are limited.
laptop.lg-gram-pro-16-16z90ts: A light 16-inch laptop at about 1.2 kg with a magnesium body and up to 20 hours of battery in light tests. The catch: keyboard travel is short and there is no fingerprint sensor.
laptop.microsoft-surface-laptop-8-13-8: A premium aluminum laptop with an excellent keyboard, haptic touchpad and bright touchscreen, with very long battery on the Snapdragon version. The catch: soldered RAM and few ports, with no card reader or HDMI.
laptop.microsoft-surface-laptop-ultra: An Arm laptop with an RTX Spark chip, a beautiful design and a haptic touchpad, suited to local AI work. The catch: it runs hot and loud under load, and single-thread speed lags.
laptop.msi-titan-18-hx-ai-a2xw: A flagship 18-inch RTX 5090 gaming laptop with top performance and a bright mini-LED screen. The catch: loud fans, a few hours of battery, a disappointing haptic touchpad and a very high price.
laptop.razer-blade-16-2026: A 16-inch RTX 5090 gaming laptop with a vivid OLED screen and long battery life for web use. The catch: it is very expensive and runs hot and loud under heavy load.
laptop.razer-blade-18-2025: A very fast 18-inch RTX 5090 gaming laptop with a dual-mode screen and a premium build. The catch: battery life is poor, fans are loud under load and the price is very high.
laptop.samsung-galaxy-book5-pro-360: A 16-inch convertible with a beautiful AMOLED touchscreen, an S Pen and very long battery life. The catch: the keyboard is shallow and multi-core CPU speed is modest.
laptop.samsung-galaxy-book6-ultra: A 16-inch laptop with a brilliant AMOLED touchscreen, a solid build and RTX 5070 graphics. The catch: the keyboard is shallow, the underside runs hot under load and every version is expensive.

discgolf.axiom-crave: Reviewers find the Crave a straight, controllable fairway driver that flips up from a hyzer and suits slower arms and wooded lines. The catch: flight varies by plastic and weight, and some run too flippy.
discgolf.innova-wraith: Flies like a more turnable, easier to throw Innova Destroyer for average to intermediate arms. The catch: stability swings a lot with plastic and weight, from flippy Pro and DX to stable Star and Champion.
discgolf.westside-harp: Reviewers find it a reliable overstable approach disc that holds forehand lines and flies much like a Discraft Zone. The catch: stability shifts noticeably between plastics and as the disc beats in.
discgolf.kastaplast-berg: Slow, glideless approach putter that holds the line it is thrown on and drops near the target. The catch: it needs real power for short distance, and some reviewers dislike putting with it.
discgolf.innova-mako3: Reviewers describe a straight, easy mid that holds the angle it is released on and works well in woods and gaps. The catch: it does not correct a flawed release and turns over on forehand.
discgolf.axiom-hex: Reviewers call the Axiom Hex a straight, shallow, comfortable mid-range with a gentle fade and plenty of glide, flying close to a Discraft Buzzz. The catch: some find it more stable than expected, and takes differ by plastic.
discgolf.innova-destroyer: Reviewers describe a stable, fading driver whose flight swings widely by plastic, weight and wear. The catch: a worn, light or Pro one can flip, and a fresh heavy one can be very overstable.
discgolf.discraft-buzzz: Reviewers find it a straight, predictable mid-range that holds its line and finishes with a little fade. The catch: flight depends heavily on plastic and wear, and it beats in toward understable.
discgolf.axiom-envy: Reviewers describe a straight-flying putter with a reliable fade and long glide, popular as a driving and approach putter. The catch: stability varies by plastic and run, and putting is not its strength.
discgolf.discraft-zone: Overstable approach putter that holds its line in wind, flexes on forehands and fades reliably, according to several reviewers. The catch: plastic changes the flight a lot, and the Z feels slick and skips.
discgolf.latitude-64-pure: Reviewers describe a shallow, beadless, neutral putter that flies straight and glides well for throwing and putting. The catch: it turns over with extra power, so hard throws and hyzers can flip.
discgolf.mvp-trail: Gives easy distance from a comfortable rim and flies close to straight, with a hyzer flip that flattens out. The catch: stability varies by plastic and run, with Proton holding more than Neutron.
discgolf.mvp-wave: A distance driver for slower to moderate arms that flips up from a hyzer and finishes with a gentle fade. The catch: it turns over hard with power, and plastic changes its stability a lot.
discgolf.latitude-64-river: Understable fairway driver with a lot of glide that reviewers find friendly to slower arms and good for distance. The catch: it can flip over easily and feel touchy, so flights are less repeatable.
discgolf.innova-teebird3: Reviewers describe a wind-handling fairway driver that runs a little faster and usually more overstable than the regular Innova TeeBird. The catch: it has less glide than the Innova TeeBird.
discgolf.mvp-detour: An understable mid that flips up to flat from a hyzer and rides straight, placed by three reviewers between the Axiom Hex and MVP Uplink. The catch: it can burn over when thrown hard.
discgolf.streamline-pilot: Flies straight with plenty of glide and holds hyzer and anhyzer lines, with a small bead. The catch: flight changes with plastic, and the premium plastics fly more overstable than Electron.
discgolf.innova-teebird: Some reviewers call it a reliable, straight fairway driver with glide and a dependable fade at the end. The catch: some find the DX flippy and the Champion much more overstable.
discgolf.mvp-tesla: Overstable 9-speed fairway driver that flies fairly straight, then fades reliably, according to many reviewers. The catch: it fades harder than the 9/5/-1/2 numbers suggest, and the flight shifts a lot by plastic and wear.
discgolf.mvp-reactor: Reviewers describe a straight to slightly overstable mid-range that holds its line and fades predictably, including on forehands. The catch: it shows little turn when new, so flippy lines need a beaten-in copy.
discgolf.axiom-insanity: Easy hyzer flips and S curves for long, controlled distance from a comfortable flat top. The catch: flight varies widely by plastic and copy, with Eclipse and Neutron flying more stable than the numbers.
discgolf.axiom-proxy: Point and shoot throwing putter that holds its line and flips to flat off a little hyzer. The catch: flatter and flippier than the Axiom Envy, with base plastics turning over more.
discgolf.axiom-pyro: Overstable, torque resistant mid-range with a reliable fade and a comfortable flat top, used for forehands, flex lines and approaches. The catch: low glide limits distance, and plastics and copies fly differently.
discgolf.discraft-luna: Glidey, round-rimmed putter used for putting, approaches and short drives, with a comfortable feel. The catch: it flies less overstable than its numbers, and stability varies a lot by plastic and run.
discgolf.dynamic-discs-judge: Beaded, glidey putter with a neutral, straight flight, trusted for putting, approaches and throwing. The catch: the bead is not for everyone.
discgolf.innova-aviar: Neutral, point and shoot putter that holds light hyzer and anhyzer lines and suits beginners. The catch: the rim runs deep for some hands, and it will not fade or turn on command.
discgolf.innova-firebird: Very overstable utility fairway driver with a dependable fade, used for forehands, flex shots, headwinds and hard hooks. The catch: it is short on distance and too overstable for slower arms.
discgolf.innova-leopard: Understable fairway driver that flies straight and long for slower arms, with easy hyzer flips and turnovers. The catch: copies turn over more as they beat in, while new Star and Champion fly more stable.
discgolf.innova-mamba: Understable distance driver that gives easy turn, hyzer flips and S curves for slower and medium arms. The catch: flight varies widely by plastic and weight, and it struggles in headwinds.
discgolf.innova-pig: Low glide, overstable approach disc whose tacky R-Pro plastic sticks where it lands and feels good on forehands. The catch: it goes only as far as it is muscled, and beat-in copies get flippier.
discgolf.latitude-64-fuse: Understable, glidey midrange that flies straight with a gentle turn and easy hyzer flips, often suggested for beginners. The catch: stability depends heavily on plastic, and it turns over with torque or power.
discgolf.innova-shryke: Very fast, wide-rimmed distance driver that flips up and turns late for long, gliding flights. The catch: it is picky about angles and arm speed, and turns too much into a headwind.
discgolf.innova-roc3: Beaded, slightly domey midrange that flies straight to overstable and holds hyzer and anhyzer lines with a reliable fade. The catch: the bead and rim feel are not for everyone, and powered forehands get squirrely.
discgolf.mvp-resistor: Slow, overstable fairway driver often called a mini Innova Firebird, flying straight then fading hard for forehands and headwinds. The catch: it is short for a fairway and its stability varies by run and plastic.
discgolf.kastaplast-reko: Rounded, low-profile putter with a micro bead that flies neutral to straight with a small finish, used for putting, approach and throwing. The catch: it flips up or turns over when thrown hard.
discgolf.mvp-volt: Slightly overstable fairway driver that pushes straight with a reliable fade, fights wind and handles forehands. The catch: flight varies by plastic and copy, and slower arms may see it hook left or dump.
discgolf.innova-valkyrie: Glidey 9-speed driver that runs from flippy DX and Star to steadier Champion and Halo. The catch: premium plastics are too stable for slow arms, and DX copies turn over for strong ones.
discgolf.innova-sidewinder: Understable 9-speed driver that flips up and finishes in an S-curve for hyzer flips, rollers and tunnels. The catch: it struggles in wind, flips over for strong arms and varies by plastic.
discgolf.innova-roc: Straight, controllable beaded midrange that holds the line it is thrown on and changes as it wears. The catch: the dome and bead feel poor to many, and flight varies by plastic and wear.
discgolf.mvp-atom: Low-profile, nearly beadless putter that flies straight with a slight finish, used for putting, upshots and short drives. The catch: stability varies by plastic and run, and the shallow rim does not suit every grip.
discgolf.axiom-tempo: Shallow, low profile approach putter that pushes straight, then fades reliably, often likened to a glidier Discraft Zone. The catch: some find it too straight, without a Zone's hard finish.
discgolf.discmania-fd: Seven-speed fairway driver with a domey top that flies straight with plenty of glide, S-Line flipping up and C-Line holding. The catch: stability swings by plastic and run, and S-Line can turn over in wind.
discgolf.discmania-p2: Deep, beadless putter that flies straight with a reliable fade, used for putting, approaches and hyzer drives. The catch: the deep rim can feel uncomfortable or wobbly, especially for smaller hands and power grips.
discgolf.innova-beast: Ten-speed distance driver that flips up from hyzer, runs straight and fades, with stability set by plastic. The catch: it can turn over into headwinds, and copies vary.
discgolf.innova-eagle: Seven-speed overstable fairway driver with a touch of turn and a hard fade for controlled hyzers and flex lines. The catch: stability varies widely by run, and beefy copies are too stable for slower arms.
discgolf.innova-leopard3: Seven-speed understable fairway driver that flips up from hyzer and holds turnover lines, friendly for beginners and slower arms. The catch: it turns and burns for faster arms and struggles in headwinds.
discgolf.innova-rhyno: Slow, overstable approach putter with a straight flight, a gentle fade and good wind resistance, used for approaches and windy putts. The catch: domed copies feel worse in hand, and it has little distance.
discgolf.innova-roadrunner: Nine-speed understable driver that flips up from hyzer and glides, easy for beginners and slower arms. The catch: it turns over when thrown hard, and stability varies by plastic and weight.
discgolf.innova-thunderbird: Nine-speed control driver with a straight flight and dependable fade, longer than an Innova TeeBird. The catch: stability varies widely by run and plastic, and new copies can be very overstable.
discgolf.kastaplast-kaxe: Six-speed hybrid between a midrange and a fairway driver, with a straight flight and dependable finish for backhand and forehand. The catch: it is less overstable than its stated numbers.
discgolf.discmania-essence: Understable 8 speed fairway driver with a lot of glide that flips up from a hyzer and gives easy distance. The catch: more power can roll it over, and flight shifts with plastic.
discgolf.kastaplast-svea: Understable midrange that flips up on hyzers and glides well. The catch: flat throws can turn over toward a roller, though one reviewer kept them straight.
discgolf.mvp-photon: Fast, stable distance driver that holds up in headwinds and finishes on a dependable hyzer fade. The catch: it can feel overstable for slower arms, and flight changes a lot by plastic.
discgolf.mvp-relay: Easy to throw 6 speed fairway driver that holds straight lines and hyzer flips in the woods. The catch: it flies more stable when fresh and does its best work once beat in.
discgolf.mvp-servo: Workable 6.5 speed fairway driver that flies straight, flips up on hyzers and finishes with a fade. The catch: stability varies by plastic, and some find it fades hard.
discgolf.mvp-watt: Straight, glidy throwing putter that holds the angle it is released on and flips up from hyzer, good for upshots and tunnels. The catch: it barely fades, which limits shot shaping.
discgolf.prodigy-a2: Very overstable approach disc with a shallow, beadless rim that hooks up quickly and resists wind. The catch: it carries little glide and drops out of the air.
discgolf.streamline-range: Low glide throwing putter that flies straight, holds its release angle and sits where it lands. The catch: it gives no correction for an off line release and gets pushed around in wind.
discgolf.streamline-trace: Straight, glidey 11 speed driver that flips up on hyzers, handles wind and gives clean forehand releases. The catch: flight swings with plastic and weight, and lighter copies turn much more than the numbers say.
discgolf.westside-tursas: Very understable midrange with a lot of glide that flips up on hyzers, easy for beginners and slower arms. The catch: anhyzers and overhand throws flip over or roll.
discgolf.discmania-md3: A straight, gliding mid that holds the line it is released on and finishes with a dependable fade. The catch: it is awkward on forehands, and new copies can feel slick or too stable.
discgolf.discraft-buzzz-ss: A straight, mildly flippy mid that holds whatever line it is thrown on and flies like a beat-in Discraft Buzzz. The catch: it turns over for bigger arms, and stability varies by plastic and run.
discgolf.discraft-heat: An understable, glidy fairway driver that gives easy distance at low power and teaches hyzer flips. The catch: it flips over easily, especially on forehands and with more power.
discgolf.gateway-wizard: An overstable, beaded putter that flies straight with a reliable fade and works for putts, upshots and short drives. The catch: the strong late fade can be too much on longer putts.
discgolf.innova-invader: A comfortable, low profile throwing putter that flies straight with a reliable fade and covers putts, approaches and short drives. The catch: copies beat in quickly and get flippy.
discgolf.innova-orc: A very stable speed 10 that holds its line and finishes left with a dependable bite. The catch: it is very overstable and resists turning over.
discgolf.innova-rat: A reliable, straight to mildly overstable approach disc that lands flat, strongest on forehand. The catch: it is more understable than the Discraft Zone, so stronger throwers may want the more stable Proto Glow.
discgolf.innova-tern: A glidy, understable speed 12 that gives easy distance on hyzer flips and S curves. The catch: it turns over hard for strong arms and is tricky on forehands.
discgolf.innova-toro: A very overstable, low glide approach disc that fights out of anhyzers and drops where it is thrown, much like the Discraft Zone. The catch: it can be too beefy for low arm speeds.
discgolf.kastaplast-falk: An understable, very glidy fairway driver with easy hyzer flips and turnovers for medium to slower arms. The catch: it turns over too much on forehands and on hard throws.
discgolf.axiom-pixel: Straight, glidey micro-bead putter that holds whatever line it is put on, for putting and throwing. The catch: the deep rim does not suit every hand, and its glide can carry it past the basket.
discgolf.kastaplast-jarn: Overstable approach disc that fades hard, fights headwinds and anhyzer, and suits forehands. The catch: it adds little for players who already trust an approach disc such as the Discraft Zone or Westside Harp.
discgolf.latitude-64-claymore: Straight, glidey midrange that releases cleanly and holds hyzer, flat and slight anhyzer lines. The catch: it holds only a modest turnover.
discgolf.latitude-64-explorer: Straight, controllable fairway driver that holds its line and finishes with a reliable fade, headwinds included. The catch: stability varies by plastic and run, so some copies fade harder or flip more.
discgolf.latitude-64-grace: Premium 11 speed driver with a fairly neutral, glidey flight that fights out of anhyzer and finishes reliably. The catch: stability varies a lot between plastics and runs, from flippy to quite overstable.
discgolf.latitude-64-saint: Glidey 9 speed control driver with a neutral to understable flight and easy distance. The catch: it is less stable than its label suggests, so stronger arms may find it turns over.
discgolf.mvp-deflector: Very overstable mid that flies fairly straight before a hard left finish, skips well and fights wind. The catch: very little glide, so it works as a situational utility disc rather than for distance.
discgolf.mvp-glitch: Light, glidey hybrid catch disc that holds any line for tight shots, jump putts and warm ups. The catch: it struggles in wind and tops out around 250 to 300 feet.
discgolf.prodigy-pa-3: Straight, beaded throwing putter that holds its line and resists torque, for putting and tight gaps alike. The catch: the prominent bead and flat, shallow feel do not suit every hand, and plastics differ.
discgolf.westside-underworld: Very understable fairway driver with a gradual right turn that makes hyzer flips, rollers and turnovers easy for slower arms. The catch: it flips easily at full power and gets flippier as it beats in.
discgolf.discmania-dd3: Fast Discmania driver that most reviewers find glidey and easy to get distance from, with flights ranging from flippy S-Line to overstable C-Line. The catch: stability varies a lot by plastic and copy.
discgolf.discmania-pd: Beefy, reliable overstable 10 speed that holds an anhyzer and fades dependably, with S-Line easier going than stiff C-Line. The catch: new C-Line copies can be too overstable for slower arms.
discgolf.dynamic-discs-escape: Glidy, controllable 9 speed fairway driver that flips to flat and fades gently, praised for beginners, hyzer flips and tight wooded lines. The catch: it turns over in headwinds and beats in toward understable.
discgolf.dynamic-discs-warden: Beadless, shallow-rimmed putter that flies straight with plenty of glide and works for putting, approaches and short drives. The catch: soft or base plastics beat in fast and can float or turn over.
discgolf.innova-boss: Fast, wide-rimmed 13 speed driver that is overstable with speed and carries big distance for strong arms. The catch: the wide rim is awkward to grip, and results vary for newer players and new copies.
discgolf.innova-gorgon: Comfortable, rounded-rim 10 speed that flips up to flat with plenty of glide, giving easy distance to slower arms. The catch: flippy plastics can burn over or roll for strong arms and in wind.
discgolf.innova-nova: Deep, grippy overmold putter that flies dead straight and holds any line, so it suits putts, approaches and form practice. The catch: the soft rim can tear or split after tree hits.
discgolf.kastaplast-lots: Smooth, grippy 9 speed that flips up from hyzer, flies straight and finishes gently, with good distance for a control driver. The catch: stability differs noticeably between runs and weights.
discgolf.latitude-64-diamond: Light, understable 8 speed that flips up and turns over easily, popular with beginners and slower arms. The catch: it burns over or rolls with any real power.
discgolf.latitude-64-saint-pro: Glidy 8 speed fairway driver with a workable mid-flight turn and dependable fade, suited to slower arms. The catch: stability changes a lot by plastic, and it turns over for faster arms.
discgolf.mvp-anode: Straight, glidey putter with a grippy feel that holds hyzer, flat and anhyzer lines. The catch: the deep rim does not suit every putting grip, and overpowered throws turn over.
discgolf.mvp-entropy: Beadless overstable putter that flies straight, then fades hard and reliably, with a comfortable feel. The catch: little glide, and some find it less overstable than marketed.
discgolf.mvp-ion: Beaded putter with a straight, stable flight that finishes with a reliable fade, and it holds anhyzer lines. The catch: it can turn over into a headwind.
discgolf.mvp-matrix: Flat-topped, beadless midrange that flies straight and torque resistant, then finishes with a fade, even into wind. The catch: low glide limits distance, with throws topping out around 300 feet.
discgolf.mvp-uplink: Understable midrange that flips up easily from hyzer, glides a long way and pans out with a slow turn. The catch: overpowered throws turn hard or roll out.
discgolf.prodigy-m4: Comfortable, glidey midrange with a flat top that holds hyzer, flat and anhyzer lines. The catch: stability varies by plastic and run, and anhyzers hold their turn without fading back.
discgolf.streamline-lift: Understable fairway driver that flips up from hyzer, turns over on anhyzer, then fades gently. The catch: Eclipse copies, especially older runs, fly much more stable than the numbers.
discgolf.westside-hatchet: Glidey, understable fairway driver with a small rim that flips to flat easily and works for rollers. The catch: big arms overpower it, and it has very little fade.
discgolf.westside-warship: Straight, neutral midrange with a domed Innova Roc-like feel and plenty of glide. The catch: only a small fade, so hyzer shots hold their line rather than finishing hard.
discgolf.axiom-paradox: Very understable mid that flips up to flat with little power and turns with almost no fade, useful for hyzer flips and rollers. The catch: it flips over easily and needs clean angles.
discgolf.discmania-origin: Flippy mid that flips up on hyzer and suits learning hyzer flips. The catch: flight varies a lot by plastic and run, and some copies fly flippier than listed.
discgolf.discraft-passion: Straight, controllable fairway driver that holds hyzer and flips up with good glide. The catch: it can turn over once beat in or with too much angle.
discgolf.dynamic-discs-emac-truth: Neutral to slightly overstable mid that flies far for a speed five and holds its release angle with a dependable fade. The catch: it can be too stable to flip on hyzer.
discgolf.dynamic-discs-felon: Flat, overstable fairway driver with a straight run before a hard fade, good for forehands and wind. The catch: stability swings a lot by plastic and wear, from beat-in straight to Lucid X very overstable.
discgolf.innova-caiman: Overstable, flat midrange with a micro bead that fades back hard and works in wind and on forehand. The catch: it leans toward advanced players and specific shots, not all-round use.
discgolf.innova-fox: Very understable, high-gliding mid that flips up with little effort and carries far, good for turnovers and hyzer flips. The catch: it can be touchy, and hard throwers or lighter copies may over-flip it.
discgolf.innova-gator: Overstable midrange that holds straight for a stretch, then hooks left hard, and copes with headwind. The catch: low glide keeps it a short range tool.
discgolf.innova-rollo: Very understable midrange that flips up from hyzer and rolls with little arm speed, suiting beginners and slow arms. The catch: it overturns easily when thrown hard and gives little fade.
discgolf.innova-tl3: Straight-flying fairway driver that holds its line and then fades. The catch: it resists turning, so it does not suit players wanting an understable disc.
discgolf.mvp-nomad: Putter with a small bead that putts well, glides far and flies fairly neutral to slightly stable. The catch: the feel does not suit everyone, whether for putting or throwing.
discgolf.prodigy-a3: Overstable approach disc that flies much like a Discraft Zone, with a little more glide and stability. The catch: it overlaps the Zone and will not hold a straight line for long.
discgolf.westside-stag: Understable-leaning fairway driver that goes straight for a long way and finishes with a fade. The catch: it flips over easily at higher power and varies a lot with plastic and wear.
discgolf.westside-sword: Flippy distance driver whose plastics cover understable to stable slots, suiting medium to slower arm speeds. The catch: flight varies a lot between plastics, domes and runs.
discgolf.axiom-aspect: Very overstable driver that reviewers compare with the Innova Thunderbird and Innova Firebird, fighting out of anhyzer. The catch: it shows little turn or flare, so it suits hyzer and flat shots.
discgolf.innova-kc-aviar: Stable, glidey beaded putter that reviewers call solid and predictable. The catch: the stiff Pro plastic feels slick and slippery in the hand, which hurts grip and release consistency.
discgolf.innova-lynx: Glidey, understable fairway driver, formerly called the IT, that reviewers find easy to throw and forgiving at slower arm speeds. The catch: forehands, especially at full power, tend to turn over into rollers.
discgolf.innova-shark: Starter set mid-range that reviewers use for approaches and putts. The catch: stability is mixed, with baseline plastic and forehand throws flipping over, so it is less dependable than its numbers suggest.
discgolf.latitude-64-brave: Understable fairway driver that flips up easily from a hyzer and holds anhyzer lines. The catch: it flies more understable than its numbers suggest, so it can turn over too easily.
discgolf.latitude-64-peak: Beaded putter that reviewers call a Latitude 64 Pure with a bead, a little more stable than the Pure. The catch: some find it too deep or too rounded over to love for putting.
discgolf.prodigy-d-model-s: Stable, fairly neutral 13 speed distance driver with a comfortable rim profile, compared by reviewers to the Prodigy D3. The catch: it suits strong arms and needs power to get the distance.
discgolf.prodigy-p-model-us: Straight putter that holds the line it is thrown on. The catch: plastic shifts the flight a little, with BaseGrip flying straighter and DuraFlex a bit more stable.
discgolf.axiom-balance: Holds straight for much of the flight, then fades, which suits wind. The catch: it runs more overstable than some players want and flies close to the Axiom Pyro.
discgolf.axiom-bokeh: Flies neutral and far, holding whatever angle it is thrown on, with easy hyzer flips and tunnel lines. The catch: reviewers trust it less on forehand, and it sits close to the Axiom Crave.
discgolf.axiom-time-lapse: Domey distance driver that goes far, with Neutron beefy and overstable and Fission flippier and glidier. The catch: Fission beats in fast, and Neutron is too overstable for some arms.
discgolf.discmania-cloud-breaker: Domey, overstable distance driver that glides and holds a line in wind. The catch: it is too much disc for shorter holes and slower arms, and the flight changes between runs.
discgolf.discmania-dd1: Controllable 11-speed that flies straight and holds up in wind, more stable than its speed suggests. The catch: it gives up some glide and distance to the Latitude 64 Grace.
discgolf.discmania-fd3: Overstable nine-speed that pushes straight before a dependable fade, that suits forehand. The catch: stability varies a lot between runs and plastics.
discgolf.discmania-function: Understable fairway driver that turns over and glides far at modest arm speeds, in tougher plastic. The catch: it turns over easily, so it suits easy throws and tricky shots more than straight ones.
discgolf.discmania-glacier: Stable mid-range that rides the line it is thrown on and flies a touch straighter than the Discmania Method. The catch: forehand throws still wobble or flip up for some reviewers.
discgolf.discmania-logic: Shallow, straight putter that holds the line it is given and handles forehand torque, with a standout hand feel. The catch: it lost some side-by-side tests to other putters on approach lines.
discgolf.discmania-premier-dd1: Flippy distance driver that goes far and holds its turn, with a thin flight plate. The catch: it burns over with power, and the thin plate feels odd in the hand.
discgolf.discmania-premier-fd: Goes far and glides well, with a stable, pushy flight that reviewers often measure against the regular Discmania FD. The catch: it runs more stable and beefier than a typical FD.
discgolf.discraft-archer: Understable driver that flips and turns easily from a hyzer release. The catch: it can flip too early or cut and roll when thrown too hard, so power needs care.
discgolf.discraft-avenger-ss: Very understable 10-speed that flips up and turns easily, which suits hyzer flips, S-curves and rollers. The catch: it is so understable that it works as a turnover disc, not a stable driver.
discgolf.discraft-captains-caliber: Stable throwing putter that sits between Discraft Luna and Discraft Zone, with a comfortable putter feel. The catch: forehand is the weak spot, where wobble can turn it over or the rim feels less secure.
discgolf.discraft-cicada: Understable, glidey fairway driver that flips up to flat and holds turnover lines. The catch: it can flip over too much, and flight varies a lot between plastics and runs.
discgolf.discraft-cigarra: Straight-flying, controllable fairway driver with a reliable finish and a comfortable rim. The catch: reviewers disagree on stability, with some finding it flippy and touchy and others finding it dead straight.
discgolf.discraft-drive: Straight-flying 11-speed that goes far with little effort and finishes with a dependable fade. The catch: it can fall out sooner than expected, especially at slower arm speeds.
discgolf.discraft-force: Very overstable, fast 12-speed driver that holds hyzer lines without flipping and suits headwinds and strong arms. The catch: it gives little distance without a lot of arm speed.
discgolf.discraft-malita: Small-diameter midrange that flies straight with plenty of glide and easy distance, close to Discraft Buzzz SS. The catch: it flies so close to Discraft Buzzz that a bag spot may be hard to justify.
discgolf.discraft-nuke: Big, fast 13-speed that goes far for strong arms and holds anhyzer lines. The catch: the large, deep rim is uncomfortable in smaller hands, and it needs a lot of arm speed.
discgolf.discraft-raptor: Overstable fairway driver with a reliable fade, compared with the Innova Firebird and used on forehands. The catch: stability varies by plastic, and some reviewers found it flipping up more than expected.
discgolf.discraft-thrasher: Understable distance driver that flips up easily and carries far at slower arm speeds, with plastic changing the stability. The catch: it is flippy, so it is a poor pick for headwinds.
discgolf.discraft-undertaker: Nine speed fairway driver with a straight flight and reliable fade that holds its line in headwinds. The catch: Titanium copies can roll over or turn flippy with age.
discgolf.discraft-zone-ss: Straight approach mid-range that flies straighter and turns over more easily than the Discraft Zone. The catch: forehands can be hard to keep consistent, and wind can cut or flip it.
discgolf.dynamic-discs-justice: Super overstable mid-range for utility shots, with a hard fade that fights wind and comes out of anhyzers. The catch: it gives up distance and glide to other mids.
discgolf.kastaplast-berg-x: Slightly more overstable Kastaplast Berg that handles forehand power better. The catch: the difference from the Kastaplast Berg is subtle for some, and it has little glide and wants to come down.
discgolf.kastaplast-idog: Seven speed fairway driver compared with the Innova TeeBird, flying straight with a little turn and a dependable fade. The catch: stability varies by run, from flippy to more stable than wanted.
discgolf.latitude-64-compass: Neutral to slightly stable mid-range that flies straight with long glide and a comfortable rim. The catch: stability differs by plastic, and reviewers disagree on how well it handles wind.
discgolf.latitude-64-rive: Stable 13 speed driver that carries far with a dependable fade and holds up in headwinds, with grippy plastic. The catch: it needs real arm speed, and a 13 speed can feel uncomfortable.
discgolf.mvp-control: Overstable driver that works as a more stable counterpart to the MVP Trail, with an early fade and a good forehand feel. The catch: it gives up some distance to the Trail.
discgolf.mvp-stasis: Overstable approach putter with little glide that holds a line and drops near the basket, often compared with the Kastaplast Berg. The catch: it falls short on long throws.
discgolf.prodigy-d1: Fast distance driver that stays stable and goes far, even in lightweight AIR plastic. The catch: stability varies between runs and weights, and it is not very overstable.
discgolf.prodigy-f9: Very understable fairway driver that flips up early and suits slower, smoother releases and hyzer flips. The catch: it is less predictable than comparable discs and rewards patience over power.
discgolf.prodigy-pa-5: Understable throwing putter that flips up easily and glides well, suited to turnovers and tight lines. The catch: it turns over when thrown hard, so angle and power need care.
discgolf.streamline-ascend: Very understable six-speed driver that flips up easily and works for pop-up turnovers and rollers. The catch: it is very understable, so it suits turnover shots and rollers more than straight drives.
discgolf.streamline-echo: Straight to slightly understable five-speed midrange that holds its line and flies far. The catch: it can run flippy, especially on forehand, and flight shifts a little between plastics and runs.
discgolf.streamline-turbulence: Overstable seven-speed fairway driver with a flat, anti-dome top that is comfortable on forehand and backhand. The catch: it does not go as far as a nine speed.
discgolf.thought-space-athletics-praxis: Throwing putter that holds the line it is put on, with a shallow shape, plenty of glide and a straight flight. The catch: stability shifts between runs and plastics.
discgolf.trash-panda-inner-core: Throwing putter that holds the line it starts on, with a straight to slightly understable flight and lots of glide. The catch: the shape and plastic can feel awkward or slick in the hand.
discgolf.climo-discs-osprey: Very understable speed 10 driver that flips and turns with little power, a fit for slower arms. The catch: it is touchy and keeps flipping when the angle is off or the throw is hard.
discgolf.dga-aftershock: Straight-flying midrange that flips up from a small hyzer and rides straight with a forward push. The catch: it has a soft finish, and faster arms can get a little turn.
discgolf.dga-avalanche: Very overstable fairway driver that flies like an Innova Firebird or Discraft Raptor and fights headwinds. The catch: it fades early with little glide, so it is not a distance disc.
discgolf.dga-banzai: Workable overstable fairway driver that flies straight, with good glide and a hard fade, and copes with headwinds. The catch: the dome and bead-like rim feel took some getting used to.
discgolf.dga-blast: Slightly more overstable approach disc than a Discraft Zone that holds anhyzer lines and fights wind. The catch: it may push less far than a Discraft Zone.
discgolf.dga-hurricane: Speed 12 distance driver and Innova Destroyer alternative that turns a little, holds its line and finishes with a strong fade, even in wind. The catch: stability varies by plastic.
discgolf.dga-quake: Overstable midrange that fights wind and takes forehand power without flipping over. The catch: it is a specialist for forehands, approaches and wind, not a disc to throw on every hole.
discgolf.dga-rift: Neutral to slightly understable midrange that flips up to flat from a hyzer and suits shaping lines in the woods. The catch: it turns a little on flat releases before the fade.
discgolf.dga-sail: Understable distance driver with lots of glide that adds distance for slower arms and handles turnovers and rollers. The catch: it takes some adjustment of release angle and power to dial in.
discgolf.dga-surf: Straight-flying putter and approach disc with a stiff, tacky feel, more stable than its minus 1 turn suggests. The catch: some find the rim deeper than expected, and glide varies between reviewers.
discgolf.dga-tsunami: Overstable 10-speed control driver that holds its line and finishes with plenty of fade. The catch: it may need extra power to flex, and at full speed it can fly less overstable than expected.
discgolf.dga-vortex: Understable fairway driver that stands up from a hyzer, glides far with little effort and makes an easy roller. The catch: flat and anhyzer releases get less use out of it.
discgolf.discraft-kratos: Luna mold with a bead: a stable, controllable putter that holds hyzer and flat lines and putts comfortably. The catch: the fade plays closer to two than three.
discgolf.doomsday-discs-chemtrail: Slightly understable fairway driver that flips up from a hyzer and rides, comfortable for lower arm speeds. The catch: hard forehands and headwinds can flip it over.
discgolf.hooligan-discs-flip: Flippy midrange that flips up and turns easily and feels comfortable in the hand. The catch: it needs the right amount of power, and forehands took more than expected to get turn.
discgolf.infinite-discs-alpaca: Stable, beadless putter that reviewers liken to the Discmania P2, with a reliable fade. The catch: the deep rim and hand feel do not suit every grip, especially for putting or sidearm.
discgolf.infinite-discs-anubis: Comfortable control midrange that holds its line on flat, hyzer and anhyzer throws. The catch: it is a straight, stable mid, so players wanting lots of turn need something flippier.
discgolf.infinite-discs-centurion: Fairway driver that carries far and flies fairly straight with a bit of fade. The catch: no review was negative, only small caveats about plastic and hand feel.
discgolf.infinite-discs-pharaoh: Speed 13 understable distance driver that flips up from a hyzer and rides far. The catch: the large rim can be uncomfortable, and it can turn touchy.
discgolf.infinite-discs-scepter: Very overstable control driver that finishes with a hard fade from every release angle and holds up in wind. The catch: new copies can feel like too much in headwinds or on power throws.
discgolf.mint-discs-jackalope: Understable 8-speed fairway driver that flips up to flat easily and suits slower arms and newer players. The catch: it flips fast, more than its numbers suggest for some, especially into a headwind.
discgolf.mint-discs-lobster: Understable 5-speed midrange that flips easily off hyzer and holds anhyzer lines around corners. The catch: the turn is strong enough that release angle and wind change the flight a lot.
discgolf.trash-panda-canyon: Overstable 4-speed midrange in gummy plastic, often compared to Discraft Zone, with a dependable fade. The catch: it is less glidy and shorter than faster overstable mids, and not for putting.
discgolf.trash-panda-dune: Straight to slightly understable 5-speed midrange with a deep, domey shape that holds the angle it is thrown on. The catch: forehand throws are less reliable and may flip up or turn.
discgolf.trash-panda-ozone: Understable 8-speed fairway driver with a lot of flip that turns over easily on hyzer flip and anhyzer lines. The catch: flat releases can turn over and tail off a long way.
discgolf.trash-panda-procyon: Stable to slightly overstable 11.5-speed distance driver that flies close to Innova Wraith. The catch: it shows little turn out of the box, so it may not flip as listed.

skin.anua-azelaic-acid-10-hyaluron-redness-so: A light, watery azelaic acid serum that reviewers found gentle and easy to layer, suited to sensitive or redness-prone skin. The catch: results on redness and pigmentation are mild and slow.
skin.anua-heartleaf-77-soothing-toner: A thin, fragrance-free, fast-absorbing toner that reviewers found gentle and calming, good for sensitive, redness-prone or oily skin. The catch: hydration and results are modest, and some saw no benefit beyond soothing.
skin.anua-rice-70-glow-milky-toner: A thin, watery rice toner that reviewers found hydrating and gentle on sensitive and acne-prone skin. The catch: it is thinner than its name suggests and can be too light for very dry, flaky skin.
skin.aveeno-calm-restore-nourishing-oat-clean: A fragrance-free, non-foaming oat gel cleanser that reviewers found very gentle and soothing, best for sensitive or irritated skin. The catch: it does not remove makeup or sunscreen and can leave a film.
skin.aveeno-calm-restore-oat-gel-moisturizer: A light, fragrance-free oat gel cream that reviewers found soothing and fast absorbing, suited to sensitive, redness-prone and oily skin. The catch: hydration is modest, so dry skin or winter needs something richer.
skin.avene-cicalfate-restorative-protective-c: A rich, fragrance-free barrier cream that reviewers love for calming redness and irritation on dry or sensitive skin. The catch: it is thick and greasy and can be too heavy for oily skin.
skin.avene-thermal-spring-water: A fragrance-free spring water spray that reviewers like for cooling and calming sensitive skin. The catch: it is pricey for plain water and has only a light effect on dry or irritated skin.
skin.avene-tolerance-extremely-gentle-cleanse: A no-rinse lotion cleanser that reviewers found gentle on dry, irritated or sensitive skin. The catch: wiped off alone it may leave the face feeling not properly cleaned, and rinsing is better day to day.
skin.axis-y-dark-spot-correcting-glow-serum: A lightweight 5% niacinamide gel serum that reviewers found gentle and easy to layer, with a subtle glow. The catch: dark spots fade slowly at best, and stubborn or sun-damaged marks barely changed.
skin.axis-y-pha-resurfacing-glow-peel: A mild PHA gel peel that reviewers found light, easy to rinse and gentle enough for sensitive skin. The catch: results are gentle and gradual rather than dramatic.
skin.axis-y-quinoa-one-step-balanced-gel-clea: A light, gentle gel cleanser that removes sunscreen and most makeup in one step without leaving skin squeaky dry. The catch: it adds no hydration, so other steps still have to do that.
skin.axis-y-vegan-collagen-eye-serum: A light, fast-absorbing hydrating eye gel that reviewers say depuffs and feels cooling. The catch: some find it not rich enough for very dry under eyes, and the applicator can feel uneven.
skin.beauty-of-joseon-dynasty-cream: A hydrating, fragrance-free cream that reviewers like for dry or normal skin but are split on for oily or acne-prone skin. The catch: it can feel sticky, and some reviewers broke out.
skin.beauty-of-joseon-ginseng-cleansing-oil: A light oil cleanser that rinses clean and melts off sunscreen and most makeup, but reviewers are divided. The catch: a strong herbal or cooking-oil scent, and it may not suit acne-prone skin.
skin.beauty-of-joseon-ginseng-essence-water: A very light, water-like ginseng toner that reviewers find gentle and hydrating enough for most skin types, sensitive included. The catch: hydration is light, so dry skin needs a moisturizer on top.
skin.beauty-of-joseon-glow-deep-serum-rice-al: A watery, scent-free serum with 2% alpha arbutin that reviewers find gentle and quick to absorb. The catch: results on dark spots are slow and uneven, and the packaging feels cheap.
skin.beauty-of-joseon-glow-replenishing-rice-: A watery, fragrance-free milky toner that hydrates lightly and absorbs fast, mostly recommended for oily and combination skin. The catch: it needs shaking before each use, and many reviewers found it merely nice.
skin.beauty-of-joseon-glow-serum-propolis-nia: A light propolis and niacinamide serum that reviewers say calms redness and breakouts, hydrates and gives a glowy finish. The catch: it is slightly sticky at first, and dark marks fade slowly.
skin.beauty-of-joseon-green-plum-refreshing-c: A mild gel cleanser that rinses clean and is gentle on sensitive skin, liked most for oily and combination skin. The catch: some find it stripping or drying, and it is weak on heavy makeup.
skin.beauty-of-joseon-green-plum-refreshing-t: A very watery exfoliating toner with mild AHA and BHA that reviewers use for texture and acne-prone skin. The catch: best kept to a few nights a week, as acids can irritate if used often.
skin.beauty-of-joseon-ground-rice-and-honey-g: A gentle rice and honey wash-off scrub mask that reviewers say leaves skin soft, bright and calm without tightness, with grit that stays mild. The catch: the rice smell is not to everyone's taste.
skin.beauty-of-joseon-matte-sun-stick-mugwort: A light, semi-matte sunscreen stick that reviewers use mainly to reapply over makeup, with no real white cast. The catch: it takes many passes to cover the face, so it suits topping up.
skin.beauty-of-joseon-red-bean-refreshing-por: A soft red bean clay mask that reviewers say does not dry out or tighten skin and leaves pores looking smoother. The catch: it does little for blackheads.
skin.beauty-of-joseon-red-bean-water-gel: A very light, cooling water gel that absorbs fast and layers under sunscreen or makeup, best liked on oily to combination skin. The catch: it can be too light for dry skin.
skin.beauty-of-joseon-relief-sun-aqua-fresh-r: A lightweight, fast-absorbing sunscreen with no white cast that reviewers say suits oily and combination skin and sits well under makeup. The catch: it is not water or sweat resistant, so it needs reapplying.
skin.beauty-of-joseon-relief-sun-rice-probiot: A light sunscreen with a soft glow and no white cast, suited to most skin types. The catch: the glow can be too much on very oily skin, and it is not water resistant.
skin.beauty-of-joseon-revive-eye-serum-ginsen: A light, fast-absorbing retinal eye serum that reviewers find gentle, with softer fine lines and a brighter look building over weeks. The catch: results are gradual, and it should be introduced slowly.
skin.bioderma-sensibio-h2o-micellar-water: A fragrance-free, gentle micellar water that reviewers say removes makeup without stinging, including on sensitive and dry skin. The catch: heavy or waterproof makeup can take several passes, and some find it pricey.
skin.byoma-milky-toner: A light, fragrance-free milky toner that reviewers say hydrates and calms sensitive skin without stickiness. The catch: it is thin and hydrates more than it moisturizes, so some do not call it a must-have.
skin.cerave-acne-foaming-cream-cleanser: A creamy 4% benzoyl peroxide acne cleanser that reviewers find fairly gentle for what it is, best suited to acne-prone skin. The catch: it barely foams and can still dry skin.
skin.cerave-am-facial-moisturizing-lotion-wit: A fragrance-free SPF 30 moisturizer that many reviewers found non-oily and easy to wear daily, including on acne-prone skin. The catch: it can leave a white tint at first and takes some rubbing in.
skin.cerave-daily-moisturizing-lotion: A light, fast-absorbing lotion for face and body that most reviewers liked for everyday use. The catch: very dry skin may want a richer cream, and acne-prone faces may break out.
skin.cerave-eye-repair-cream: A light, fragrance-free eye cream that reviewers found comfortable and hydrating, including on sensitive eyes. The catch: it does little for dark circles or puffiness.
skin.cerave-foaming-facial-cleanser: A fragrance-free gel foaming cleanser that reviewers liked for oily, combination and acne-prone skin, cleaning without stripping or drying. The catch: heavy makeup needs a second wash or a pre-cleanse.
skin.cerave-healing-ointment: A petrolatum ointment that reviewers loved for night-time slugging, dry flaky skin and chapped lips. The catch: it is sticky at first and can be a poor fit for acne-prone skin.
skin.cerave-hydrating-cream-to-foam-cleanser: A fragrance-free, gentle cream cleanser that foams a little and takes off light makeup and sunscreen without stripping skin. The catch: it does not remove heavy or waterproof makeup in one wash.
skin.cerave-hydrating-facial-cleanser: A gentle, fragrance-free, non-foaming cleanser that reviewers liked for normal to dry and sensitive skin, leaving it soft. The catch: it is weak on makeup and oil, so heavy makeup and oily skin need more.
skin.cerave-moisturizing-cream: A thick, fragrance-free cream that reviewers loved for dry, flaky and eczema-prone skin on the face and body. The catch: it is heavy, so oily or acne-prone faces may not suit it.
skin.cerave-pm-facial-moisturizing-lotion: A very light, fragrance-free lotion that absorbs fast and suits combination and oily skin as a bedtime or all-day moisturizer. The catch: it stung or burned some sensitive skin, and dry skin may want more.
skin.cerave-renewing-sa-cleanser: A fragrance-free salicylic acid gel cleanser that most reviewers liked for oily, acne-prone or bumpy skin, with gentle exfoliation. The catch: it can sting or irritate dry, sensitive or rosacea-prone skin.
skin.cerave-resurfacing-retinol-serum: A light, gel-like retinol serum that reviewers find gentle and easy to start with, mainly for post-acne marks and uneven tone. The catch: the retinol strength is not printed on the bottle.
skin.cerave-skin-renewing-night-cream: A thick, fragrance-free night cream that reviewers find very hydrating, with a soft, plump feel by morning. The catch: it can feel too heavy or clog pores on very oily or acne-prone skin.
skin.cerave-skin-renewing-vitamin-c-serum: A hydrating 10% L-ascorbic acid serum that reviewers find easy to tolerate and often suggest for first-time vitamin C users. The catch: it oxidizes and darkens quickly, so use the tube up within months.
skin.cerave-ultra-light-moisturizing-lotion-s: A lightweight chemical-filter sunscreen lotion with no white cast that reviewers find easy to wear, especially on oily and combination skin. The catch: very dry skin may find it not moisturizing enough.
skin.cetaphil-gentle-skin-cleanser: A mild, low-foam cleanser that reviewers find gentle and non-drying, best for dry or sensitive skin. The catch: it barely lathers and can feel under-cleansing on oily or acne-prone skin.
skin.cetaphil-hydrating-eye-gel-cream: A light, quick-absorbing eye gel-cream that reviewers find comfortable and good under concealer. The catch: it did little for dark circles, puffiness or bags, and may not hydrate dry or aging eyes enough.
skin.cetaphil-moisturizing-cream: A thick, rich cream that reviewers find very hydrating and gentle, even on sensitive or acne-prone skin. The catch: it is very thick, and may not suit oily skin in summer.
skin.cosrx-acne-pimple-master-patch: Hydrocolloid patches that reviewers say stay on overnight and work best on whiteheads and pimples that already have a head. The catch: they do little for closed, deep spots.
skin.cosrx-advanced-snail-92-all-in-one-cream: A fragrance-free snail mucin gel-cream that reviewers find hydrating and soothing, with a dewy glow. The catch: the tacky, slimy texture is slow to absorb, and dry skin needs a richer cream on top.
skin.cosrx-advanced-snail-96-mucin-power-esse: A slimy, slightly sticky snail mucin essence that reviewers find very hydrating and gentle, with a glossy finish. The catch: it needs a moisturizer on top and does little for acne marks.
skin.cosrx-advanced-snail-peptide-eye-cream: A light, fragrance free eye cream that hydrates and sits well under makeup, good for sensitive eye areas. The catch: dark circles and fine lines do not change much.
skin.cosrx-aha-7-whitehead-power-liquid: A 7% glycolic acid liquid that reviewers use once or a few times a week for smoother skin and small bumps. The catch: it can sting or redden skin, and whitehead results vary.
skin.cosrx-aha-bha-clarifying-treatment-toner: A gentle, watery spray toner with glycolic acid and betaine salicylate, liked for smaller-looking pores and slightly clearer skin without irritation. The catch: it is too mild for some.
skin.cosrx-aloe-soothing-sun-cream-spf-50: A creamy, hydrating SPF 50 that most reviewers found free of white cast, best for dry to normal skin. The catch: noticeable fragrance and alcohol, and pilling or heaviness for some.
skin.cosrx-balancium-comfort-ceramide-cream: A thick, balm-like ceramide cream that hydrates dry, dehydrated or irritated skin, best at night or in cold weather. The catch: heavy under sunscreen and for oily skin, plus a bergamot scent.
skin.cosrx-bha-blackhead-power-liquid: A watery, gentle BHA with betaine salicylate that hydrates and suits exfoliation beginners, with fewer blackheads for some. The catch: results are mild and slow, and some saw no change.
skin.cosrx-full-fit-propolis-synergy-toner: A soothing, hydrating propolis toner with a soft glow, liked on dry, dehydrated and sensitive skin. The catch: a slightly sticky feel when layered, and it is not for very oily skin or propolis allergies.
skin.cosrx-low-ph-good-morning-gel-cleanser: A gentle, low pH tea tree gel cleanser that cleans without tightness, mostly liked on oily, combination and sensitive skin. The catch: it is not very hydrating and does not remove waterproof makeup.
skin.cosrx-one-step-original-clear-pad: A gentle BHA pad liked for smaller, cleaner-looking pores, without dryness or stinging. The catch: the scent ranges from subtle citrus to strongly medicinal, and reviewers mostly report pore changes.
skin.cosrx-salicylic-acid-daily-gentle-cleans: A gentle, creamy 0.5% salicylic acid cleanser that foams richly and suits oily, acne-prone skin used daily. The catch: visible results take a few weeks of steady use.
skin.cosrx-the-6-peptide-skin-booster-serum: A watery, scent-free first-step serum that reviewers mostly liked for its light feel, fast absorption and gentleness. The catch: the results are subtle, and several felt it did little beyond hydrating.
skin.cosrx-the-ceramide-skin-barrier-moisturi: A fragrance-free ceramide cream liked for non-greasy hydration on dry, sensitive and combination skin. The catch: it can feel too light for dry skin in cold weather or heavy for oily skin by day.
skin.cosrx-the-retinol-0-1-cream: A lightweight beginner retinol cream that reviewers found gentle and quick to sink in. The catch: the tube is small, and results build slowly.
skin.cosrx-the-retinol-0-5-oil: A squalane-based retinol oil that reviewers found gentle and smooth, with no irritation reported. The catch: it needs a slow start, every other night at first.
skin.cosrx-ultimate-nourishing-rice-overnight: A fragrance-free gel-cream sleeping mask that reviewers liked as a gentle, hydrating night step, also used by some as a moisturizer. The catch: brightening is slight, and it can feel heavy on oily skin.
skin.cosrx-ultra-light-invisible-sunscreen-sp: A lightweight, scent-free chemical sunscreen with no white cast that reviewers liked for daily wear under makeup. The catch: it is not water or sweat resistant, so it suits daily wear, not swimming.
skin.drunk-elephant-a-passioni-retinol-cream: A strong 1% retinol cream that most reviewers found effective for texture and pigmentation once introduced slowly. The catch: the strength brings dryness, peeling and irritation, and the tube squeezes out too much.
skin.drunk-elephant-b-hydra-intensive-hydrati: A watery hydrating gel serum that reviewers found fast-absorbing and gentle, with a glow and good layering under moisturizer. The catch: it is pricey, and some found little lasting hydration from it.
skin.drunk-elephant-lala-retro-whipped-cream: A whipped, fragrance-free midweight moisturizer that reviewers found pleasant and mostly non-irritating. The catch: hydration is basic for the cost, and acne-prone or oily skin may find it greasy or breakout-prone.
skin.drunk-elephant-t-l-c-framboos-glycolic-n: An AHA and BHA night gel that reviewers mostly liked for steady texture help and well-made packaging. The catch: it is pricey, and it can dry or irritate dry skin.
skin.eltamd-uv-clear-broad-spectrum-spf-46: A light, easy-to-spread daily sunscreen that suited oily, combination and redness-prone skin for several reviewers, though opinion was split. The catch: some felt tingling or burning, and some saw a white cast.
skin.eltamd-uv-physical-broad-spectrum-spf-41: A lightly tinted mineral sunscreen with a natural matte finish that reviewers mostly liked. The catch: it can look pale or leave a cast on darker skin, and it can peel when layered.
skin.eltamd-uv-restore-broad-spectrum-spf-40: A hydrating mineral sunscreen with squalane that suits dry or dehydrated skin, though reviewers were only partly sold. The catch: it can leave a white cast, and some found it not worth the money.
skin.eucerin-clear-skin-spf-50-face-sunscreen: A chemical SPF 50 oil-control face lotion with no white cast that works fine under makeup. The catch: reviewers disagreed on oil control, with some finding it shiny, heavy or filmy.
skin.first-aid-beauty-pure-skin-face-cleanser: A gentle, fragrance-free cream cleanser that foams lightly and was liked by reviewers with sensitive or dry skin. The catch: heavy makeup, foundation and mascara may need extra passes or a second cleanse.
skin.first-aid-beauty-ultra-repair-cream: A thick, hydrating cream with colloidal oatmeal that reviewers liked for dry, sensitive or irritated skin. The catch: it can feel too heavy in summer, especially on oily or combination skin.
skin.glow-recipe-avocado-ceramide-moisture-ba: A gentle, creamy cleanser with a light lather that leaves skin neither tight nor dry, liked on sensitive and combination skin. The catch: it has a light scent that may not suit fragrance allergies.
skin.glow-recipe-guava-vitamin-c-bright-eye-g: A hydrating gel-cream eye product with a pump and light fruity scent that reviewers liked for brighter-looking, less puffy under eyes. The catch: it is pricey for the amount of product.
skin.glow-recipe-plum-plump-hyaluronic-cream: A light gel cream with strong hydration and a refillable pod, liked for normal and combination skin. The catch: it can feel too light for dry winter skin, and oily and combination skin responded differently.
skin.glow-recipe-strawberry-smooth-bha-aha-sa: A gentle, hydrating BHA and AHA gel serum that reviewers liked for acne-prone and sensitive skin and as a mild first acid. The catch: it contains fragrance, and results can be modest.
skin.glow-recipe-watermelon-glow-aha-night-tr: A gel night treatment with an AHA that reviewers found gentle, hydrating and smoothing, even on sensitive skin. The catch: the scent is only okay, and a couple felt brief redness or stinging.
skin.glow-recipe-watermelon-glow-jelly-sheet-: A two-piece hydrogel sheet mask that reviewers found cooling and hydrating, with a watermelon scent and a glow afterwards. The catch: the delicate sheet slides around and tears easily.
skin.glow-recipe-watermelon-glow-niacinamide-: A dewy niacinamide serum that reviewers use as a glow booster or makeup primer. The catch: some find it sticky or tacky, and some see it as more primer than treatment.
skin.glow-recipe-watermelon-glow-pha-bha-pore: A syrupy, hydrating toner with PHA and BHA that reviewers found gentle. The catch: the exfoliation is light and pores did not visibly tighten, and the scent is only okay.
skin.glow-recipe-watermelon-glow-ultra-fine-m: A very fine, watermelon-scented mist reviewers use between skincare steps or as a refresher. The catch: value is rated low, and it does not make makeup last longer.
skin.haruharu-wonder-black-rice-hyaluronic-to: A thick, very hydrating toner with a lavender scent that leaves skin soft and supple. The catch: it gets tacky when layered, and the alcohol and fragrance may bother sensitive skin.
skin.haruharu-wonder-black-rice-moisture-airy: A moisturizing SPF 50+ chemical sunscreen with no white cast or scent that most reviewers loved under makeup. The catch: it is not water resistant, and oily or sensitive skin may struggle.
skin.kiehls-ultra-facial-cream: A creamy, lightweight moisturizer that reviewers found very hydrating for dry skin and that layers well under makeup. The catch: the jar is less hygienic, and some find it pricey for the formula.
skin.kravebeauty-beet-the-sun-spf-40: A lightweight, hydrating chemical sunscreen with a dewy finish and no white cast. The catch: it turns shiny on oily skin, and SPF 40 with older filters is not for everyone.
skin.kravebeauty-great-barrier-relief: A creamy barrier serum that reviewers found soothing for irritated, compromised skin. The catch: the natural smell is off-putting, and it is meant to sit under a moisturizer, not replace one.
skin.kravebeauty-kale-lalu-yaha: A gentle glycolic acid liquid that reviewers found quick to absorb and good for people new to AHAs. The catch: a mild sting or tingle on application.
skin.kravebeauty-matcha-hemp-hydrating-cleans: A jelly-like gel cleanser that reviewers found hydrating and gentle, with no stripping or tightness. The catch: it is not a strong makeup remover, so full makeup calls for a first cleanse.
skin.la-roche-posay-anthelios-melt-in-milk-su: A light, quick-absorbing SPF 60 lotion with no white cast that reviewers liked for face and body, from oily to dry skin. The catch: value is only okay for some reviewers.
skin.la-roche-posay-cicaplast-balm-b5: A thick overnight balm that reviewers found soothing on dry, irritated or retinoid-stressed skin. The catch: it is very rich, so it suits oily or breakout-prone skin less well.
skin.la-roche-posay-effaclar-gel-cleanser-for: A clear gel cleanser that reviewers found foams well and cleans oily to combination skin gently. The catch: it can feel tight or drying, especially if used twice a day or on dry skin.
skin.la-roche-posay-retinol-b3-pure-retinol-s: A gentle retinol and niacinamide serum that most reviewers found easy on sensitive skin, with brighter, more even skin after weeks. The catch: fragrance and dropper packaging let it down, and results take months.
skin.la-roche-posay-toleriane-double-repair-f: A light, almost unscented moisturizer that reviewers found hydrating and gentle on sensitive skin. The catch: it can pill under sunscreen or makeup, and some found it not hydrating enough.
skin.la-roche-posay-toleriane-hydrating-gentl: A fragrance-free, lotion-like cleanser that reviewers found hydrating and gentle for normal, dry and sensitive skin. The catch: it does not remove makeup, and some think oily skin may not like it.
skin.la-roche-posay-toleriane-purifying-foami: A light foaming gel cleanser that reviewers found gentle and non-irritating on normal to oily, combination and acne-prone skin. The catch: dry skin may get drier, so it suits dry skin less well.
skin.laneige-cream-skin-toner-moisturizer: A milky, fragrance-free toner and moisturizer hybrid that reviewers found hydrating and gentle, especially for dry skin. The catch: it can feel too rich or greasy on oily skin in summer.
skin.laneige-water-sleeping-mask: A water-based jelly sleeping mask that reviewers mostly found plumping and soft by morning. The catch: the fragrance can bother sensitive skin, and a few reviewers broke out or found it drying.
skin.mario-badescu-drying-lotion: A pink sulfur spot treatment that reviewers found dries and shrinks pimples within a day or two. The catch: it is weaker on deep cystic spots and not a true overnight fix.
skin.mario-badescu-facial-spray-with-aloe-her: A rose-scented mist reviewers use to refresh skin and set makeup, mostly with no breakouts or irritation. The catch: the rose scent is strong for some, and it is more refresher than treatment.
skin.mario-badescu-super-collagen-mask: A clay-style mask that dries firm and rinses off, which reviewers found gentle on sensitive skin with a pleasant, clean scent. The catch: results are modest and it dries very tight.
skin.missha-time-revolution-the-first-essence: A watery, scentless first essence that absorbs fast, which reviewers mostly liked for hydration and glow. The catch: some find it watered down next to older versions, and it can sting at first.
skin.mixsoon-bean-cream: A lightweight fermented-bean cream that reviewers found very hydrating without a greasy feel, suited to dry through combination skin. The catch: the bergamot and lavender oils may irritate sensitive skin.
skin.mixsoon-bean-essence: A stretchy, fragrance-free fermented essence that reviewers liked for glow and smoother skin, often as a snail mucin alternative. The catch: it is less hydrating than snail mucin, so weaker for very dry skin.
skin.naturium-bha-liquid-exfoliant-2: A gentle, lightweight 2% salicylic acid exfoliant that reviewers found hydrating and non-irritating. The catch: some reviewers still prefer Paula's Choice SKIN PERFECTING 2% BHA Liquid Exfoliant.
skin.naturium-dew-glow-moisturizer-spf-50: A creamy, dewy SPF 50 moisturizer that reviewers liked for dry skin and winter, with no white cast. The catch: it looks greasy on oily skin, and reviewers warn acne-prone skin away from it.
skin.naturium-glycolic-acid-resurfacing-gel-1: A 10% glycolic acid gel that reviewers found gentle, without burning, when used once or twice a week. The catch: it is easy to overdo.
skin.naturium-mandelic-topical-acid-12: A gentle 12% mandelic acid exfoliant with niacinamide, liked by reviewers for sensitive skin and people new to acids. The catch: it is a mild exfoliant, so it suits gentle use more than strong results.
skin.naturium-multi-peptide-eye-cream: A peptide eye cream with a silky, emollient feel that reviewers find moisturizing and gentle. The catch: it does little beyond hydration, and it did not help dark circles.
skin.naturium-retinaldehyde-cream-serum: A retinal cream serum that absorbs quickly and, at the 0.10% strength, was found gentle with little irritation. The catch: beginners are advised to start with the lower 0.05% strength first.
skin.neutrogena-hydro-boost-eye-gel-cream: A light, cooling eye gel-cream that reviewers found hydrating, fast-absorbing and free of irritation on dry or sensitive under-eyes. The catch: none stood out across the reviews.
skin.neutrogena-hydro-boost-gel-cream-extra-d: A fragrance free gel cream that feels light but hydrating and absorbs quickly, suited to dry skin. The catch: reviewers noted slight irritation, stinging or possible breakouts for some skin.
skin.neutrogena-hydro-boost-hyaluronic-acid-w: A watery, fast-absorbing hyaluronic gel moisturizer that reviewers like for oily and combination skin, with no greasy feel or shine. The catch: hydration can fade for dry skin, and it irritated sensitive skin for some.
skin.neutrogena-oil-free-acne-wash: A 2% salicylic acid acne wash that reviewers say can clear oily, acne-prone skin. The catch: it is drying and often irritating, so most reviewers had dryness, burning or rashes.
skin.numbuzin-no-3-super-glowing-essence-tone: A fermented essence toner that gives a hydrating glow, liked most on dull or dry skin. The catch: a strong rose or herbal scent, and a thick feel that is heavy on oily skin.
skin.numbuzin-no-5-glutathione-vitamin-concen: A lightweight brightening serum with vitamin C derivatives, glutathione and niacinamide that reviewers found gentle and easy to layer. The catch: results are gradual and modest, so it needs patience and consistency.
skin.numbuzin-no-9-nad-retinal-volumetox-eye-: A retinal eye cream with a medium-weight, hydrating texture and a glowing finish, gentle enough for sensitive eyes. The catch: it needs a slow start, and very dark circles may need more help.
skin.paulas-choice-10-azelaic-acid-booster: A light cream-gel with azelaic and salicylic acid for acne-prone, combination skin, praised for texture and for calming redness and marks. The catch: the salicylic acid can irritate reactive skin.
skin.paulas-choice-c5-super-boost-eye-cream: A light, fast-absorbing vitamin C eye cream, liked for hydration, brightening and little or no irritation. The catch: the brightening is modest, not a full fix for dark circles.
skin.paulas-choice-clinical-0-3-retinol-2-bak: A mid-strength retinol with bakuchiol and peptides, liked as a gentler step into retinol for sensitive or cautious skin. The catch: it is on the pricey side.
skin.paulas-choice-clinical-1-retinol-treatme: A strong 1% retinol with peptides, liked by those who build up slowly and add a rich moisturizer. The catch: it is strong and can irritate, so it needs a slow build up.
skin.paulas-choice-resist-advanced-replenishi: A nourishing toner that softens skin and gives lasting hydration, liked on combination to dry skin. The catch: it can feel rich, and sensitive skin reacted badly for one reviewer.
skin.paulas-choice-resist-youth-extending-dai: A thin chemical SPF 50 fluid with little white cast that sits well under makeup, liked for oily to normal skin. The catch: it can sting the eyes.
skin.paulas-choice-skin-balancing-pore-reduci: A light, watery toner for normal, combination and oily skin, liked for a fresh feel with no irritation. The catch: it hydrates only lightly, so dry skin may want more.
skin.paulas-choice-skin-perfecting-2-bha-gel-: A 2% salicylic acid gel liked for clearing pores, whiteheads and dark spots on acne-prone skin. The catch: it can leave skin tight, and the texture and smell are only okay.
skin.paulas-choice-skin-perfecting-2-bha-liqu: A gentle, fragrance-free leave-on 2% salicylic acid liquid, liked for pores, breakouts and congestion across skin types. The catch: it is best built up slowly, since daily use can redden, dry or irritate.
skin.paulas-choice-skin-perfecting-8-aha-gel-: An 8% glycolic acid gel used a few nights a week for smoother, more even skin and glow. The catch: it can sting, dry the skin and needs keeping apart from retinol.
skin.paulas-choice-skin-recovery-enriched-cal: A lightweight, hydrating toner that calms dry or irritated skin and absorbs quickly. The catch: reviewers found little to fault.
skin.peach-lily-glass-skin-refining-serum: A light, fragrance-free gel serum that hydrates fast and leaves skin dewy without feeling greasy. The catch: reviewers named few drawbacks.
skin.peach-slices-acne-spot-dots: Translucent spot patches in three sizes that stay discreet overnight and leave pimples smaller and less red. The catch: they are hard to peel off the sheet, and sticking is only so-so.
skin.skin1004-centella-toning-toner: A watery, fragrance-free PHA toner that absorbs fast and soothes, gentle enough for oily, sensitive or acne-prone skin. The catch: the exfoliation is mild and results can be slow or plain.
skin.skin1004-hyalu-cica-water-fit-sun-serum: A very light, fragrance-free chemical sunscreen with a dewy glow and no white cast. The catch: it is not sweat or water resistant, and the dewiness may be too much for oily skin.
skin.skin1004-madagascar-centella-ampoule: A very watery, fragrance-free centella ampoule that absorbs fast and gradually calms redness and irritation, for sensitive or oily skin. The catch: hydration is light, so dry skin needs a richer cream on top.
skin.skin1004-poremizing-quick-clay-stick-mas: A mess-free clay stick that glides on and rinses off, gentle for many but drying for some. The catch: results on clogged pores are mild, and the small stick runs out fast.
skin.skin1004-probio-cica-bakuchiol-eye-cream: A rich yet fast-absorbing bakuchiol eye cream that hydrates dry or dehydrated under-eyes and softly brightens. The catch: the mixed reviewers hit occasional stinging or weaker results on dark circles and fine lines.
skin.stratia-soft-touch-aha: A gentle 10% mandelic acid gel that smooths and brightens skin with little irritation, suited to sensitive skin and exfoliation beginners. The catch: reviewers found little to fault.
skin.stratia-velvet-cleansing-milk: A gentle, fragrance-free milky cleanser that leaves skin comfortable and hydrated, with no foam or tightness. The catch: it is weak at removing makeup, so some reviewers pair it with an oil or balm first.
skin.sunday-riley-a-high-dose-retinoid-serum: A light, quick-absorbing retinoid serum that most reviewers found gentle, a good fit for people new to retinoids. The catch: the strength is milder than the name suggests, and the smell divides.
skin.sunday-riley-auto-correct-brightening-de: A lightweight, hydrating eye cream with a slight shimmer, liked for a brighter, fresher look under the eyes. The catch: results are modest for some, a few found it irritating, and it is pricey.
skin.sunday-riley-c-e-o-15-vitamin-c-brighten: A light, lotion-like vitamin C serum with a citrus scent that absorbs fast and brightens a little. The catch: results are modest for most reviewers, and citrus oils may bother sensitive skin.
skin.sunday-riley-good-genes-lactic-acid-trea: A light, lotion-like lactic acid treatment that most reviewers found brightening and smoothing. The catch: lemongrass oil and low pH bring tingling or irritation for some, and the smell divides.
skin.sunday-riley-u-f-o-acne-treatment-face-o: A light salicylic acid face oil that settled pimples in days for several reviewers with oily, blemish-prone or sensitive skin. The catch: the smell and green color put many off, and some broke out.
skin.supergoop-bright-eyed-mineral-eye-cream-: A mineral SPF eye cream with a light pink or peachy tint that visibly brightens the under eyes. The catch: it can pill, flake or peel under makeup, so it needs time to dry down.
skin.supergoop-glowscreen-spf-40: A glowy, hydrating chemical sunscreen with a tint that most reviewers liked as a makeup primer. The catch: it is very shimmery for use alone, not water resistant, and stings or peels for some.
skin.supergoop-mineral-mattescreen-spf-40: A whipped, tinted mineral sunscreen with a smooth matte finish and no white cast, liked on oily, combination and sensitive skin. The catch: the tint gives only light coverage.
skin.supergoop-play-everyday-lotion-spf-50: A creamy SPF 50 lotion for face and body that rubs in with no white cast and little irritation. The catch: it feels tacky or greasy at first and leaves some shine.
skin.supergoop-unseen-sunscreen-spf-50: A clear, silky gel SPF 50 with no scent or white cast that works as a soft-matte primer. The catch: it works best in one thin layer.
