skin.tatcha-the-dewy-skin-cream: A rich jar cream with a dewy finish that suits dry to combination skin and feels well packaged. The catch: it is thick and scented, so oily skin may find it too heavy.
skin.tatcha-the-rice-wash: A creamy cleanser that foams softly, with very mild rice-grain exfoliation, and cleans without stripping for most reviewers. The catch: it is fragranced and pricey for a cleanser.
skin.tatcha-the-silk-sunscreen-spf-50: A light, runny mineral SPF 50 with a dewy or satin finish that sits well under makeup with little to no white cast. The catch: it is pricey for a sunscreen.
skin.tatcha-the-water-cream: A light, fast-absorbing gel-cream with a matte-satin finish that suits normal, combination and oily skin and sits well under makeup. The catch: hydration can fall short for very dry skin or winter.
skin.the-inkey-list-10-azelaic-acid-serum: A light, green-tinted azelaic acid serum that absorbs fast and is gentle on redness-prone skin. The catch: redness results are slow or small for some reviewers.
skin.the-inkey-list-beta-hydroxy-acid-bha-ser: A thin, fragrance-free leave-on salicylic acid serum that reviewers found useful for blackheads and blemishes on oily or congested skin. The catch: it is not very hydrating, so it suits dry skin poorly.
skin.the-inkey-list-caffeine-eye-cream: A lightweight, fast-absorbing, scent-free eye cream that layers well and sits nicely under makeup. The catch: puffiness barely changed for some reviewers, and it reads as a good moisturizer rather than a treatment.
skin.the-inkey-list-glycolic-acid-toner: A watery 10% glycolic acid toner that absorbs fast and suits oilier skin, with a pleasant scent. The catch: witch hazel and alcohol can leave it drying and stinging, so start slowly.
skin.the-inkey-list-hyaluronic-acid-serum: A lightweight, scent-free 2% hyaluronic acid serum that is good value and layers well under moisturizer. The catch: it works as a booster and needs a moisturizer or sealing layer on top.
skin.the-inkey-list-oat-cleansing-balm: A fragrance-free oat balm that melts makeup and feels calming and hydrating on sensitive skin, best as a first cleanse. The catch: it can leave a film and needs a second cleanse or cloth.
skin.the-inkey-list-pha-toner: A gentle, fragrance-free exfoliating toner that absorbs fast and suits sensitive or easily irritated skin. The catch: the exfoliation is mild, so results are modest for oily or texture-prone skin.
skin.the-inkey-list-retinol-eye-cream: A fragrance-free, very gentle retinol eye cream that suits people nervous about retinol near the eyes. The catch: fine lines changed little for several reviewers, and some found it short on moisture.
skin.the-inkey-list-salicylic-acid-cleanser: A gentle, clear gel cleanser with salicylic acid that cleans without stripping, aimed at oily, acne-prone skin. The catch: results for breakouts are modest, and some reviewers dislike the smell or the bottle.
skin.the-inkey-list-succinic-acid-treatment: A green-tinted spot treatment that most reviewers say calms redness and shrinks inflamed pimples within a day or two. The catch: it tints skin green, and its star ingredient is oversold.
skin.the-inkey-list-tranexamic-acid-serum: A light gel for fading newer post-acne marks and mild uneven tone. The catch: results are slow, and it does little for old or stubborn pigmentation.
skin.the-ordinary-100-plant-derived-squalane: A very light, fragrance-free squalane oil that sinks in fast and layers under makeup or moisturizer. The catch: it still feels like an oil, which a few reviewers did not like.
skin.the-ordinary-aha-30-bha-2-peeling-soluti: A strong at-home peel used about once a week for brighter, smoother skin and fading acne marks. The catch: it can burn or redden skin, so start short and patch test.
skin.the-ordinary-ascorbyl-glucoside-solution: A gentle, fragrance-free vitamin C serum that absorbs quickly and suits sensitive skin and first-time vitamin C users. The catch: brightening is mild and slow, and the texture can turn tacky or pill.
skin.the-ordinary-azelaic-acid-suspension-10: A budget azelaic acid treatment that reviewers use for redness, post-acne marks and dark spots. The catch: the thick, silicone-heavy texture can feel drying or ball up on skin.
skin.the-ordinary-caffeine-solution-5-egcg: A light caffeine eye serum that many use to depuff and brighten under-eyes within weeks. The catch: it does little for genetic bags or hollows, and can feel sticky.
skin.the-ordinary-glucoside-foaming-cleanser: A gentle foaming gel that cleans oily and combination skin without stripping and removes sunscreen well. The catch: it will not remove heavy or waterproof makeup.
skin.the-ordinary-glycolic-acid-7-exfoliating: A watery 7% glycolic acid toner that brings a glow, smoother skin and slowly fading marks. The catch: frequent use can irritate, so reviewers keep to a few nights a week with sunscreen.
skin.the-ordinary-glycolipid-cream: A non-foaming gel-cream cleanser that is very gentle and removes sunscreen and light makeup, best for dry or sensitive skin. The catch: heavy or waterproof makeup needs a first cleanse with an oil or balm.
skin.the-ordinary-granactive-retinoid-2-emuls: A light, milky retinoid emulsion that is gentle and easy to absorb, suited to beginners and sensitive skin. The catch: results are mild and slow, so retinoid veterans may want something stronger.
skin.the-ordinary-granactive-retinoid-5-in-sq: A gentle, fragrance-free retinoid in a squalane base that suits beginners and sensitive skin and slowly evens tone. The catch: it feels oily and results are slow and subtle.
skin.the-ordinary-hyaluronic-acid-2-b5: A hydrating gel serum that reviewers like most in its reformulated version, which is lighter, less sticky and has ceramides. The catch: some still find mild tackiness or a faint film.
skin.the-ordinary-lactic-acid-10-ha: A gentle leave-on lactic acid exfoliant that brings a glow and smoother skin, suited to dry or sensitive skin. The catch: results come slowly and it needs spacing from retinoids and other acids.
skin.the-ordinary-multi-peptide-eye-serum: A very thin, light, fragrance-free peptide eye serum that absorbs fast and gives a subtle depuffed, brighter look. The catch: results are modest, and dry skin needs a richer cream on top.
skin.the-ordinary-multi-peptide-ha-serum: A water-based peptide and hyaluronic acid serum that reviewers use for hydration, plumpness and a soft, fresh look. The catch: results are modest and it can feel tacky until moisturiser goes on.
skin.the-ordinary-natural-moisturizing-factor: A light, fragrance-free, oil-free gel moisturizer that hydrates without grease, best for oily, combination and acne-prone skin. The catch: it is too light for dry skin, and the hydration may not last.
A fragrance-free basic cream that most reviewers found gentle and non-greasy, best for normal to combination skin. The catch: it can feel thick and slow to sink in, and very dry skin needs extra.
skin.the-ordinary-niacinamide-10-zinc-1: An inexpensive 10% niacinamide serum that some reviewers credit with smoother, brighter skin and less shine, mostly on oily to combination skin. The catch: the strength can tingle, dry or irritate, so start slowly.
skin.the-ordinary-retinal-0-2-emulsion: A strong, fragrance-free retinal emulsion that most reviewers liked for smoother, brighter skin. The catch: it is too intense for beginners and sensitive skin, and the small 15 ml bottle does not last.
skin.the-ordinary-retinol-0-5-in-squalane: A mid-strength retinol in a squalane oil base that reviewers found smoothing, best for people with some retinol experience. The catch: it feels oily, sinks in slowly and needs a slow start.
skin.the-ordinary-saccharomyces-ferment-30-mi: A thin, milky, yeast-based toner that most reviewers found gentle and hydrating and quick to sink in. The catch: exfoliating and brightening effects are mild, and some reviewers found it thin or irritating.
skin.the-ordinary-salicylic-acid-2-anhydrous-: A squalane-based salicylic acid serum that most reviewers found gentle and hydrating, suiting sensitive, dry and acne-prone skin. The catch: it feels oily and can sit heavy on oily skin or under makeup.
skin.the-ordinary-salicylic-acid-2-masque: A clay rinse-off mask that reviewers liked for cleaning out pores and blackheads on oily, blemish-prone skin. The catch: it is messy to apply and rinse off, and can tingle or leave skin tight.
skin.the-ordinary-salicylic-acid-2-solution: A water-based 2% salicylic acid solution that reviewers liked for clearing blackheads and pimples on oily to combination skin. The catch: it can foam, pill and dry out dry or sensitive skin.
skin.the-ordinary-soothing-barrier-support-se: A fragrance-free pink serum that reviewers found hydrating and calming on irritated, dry or sensitive skin. The catch: the dropper is fiddly, the pink tint puts some off, and it is not a must-have.
skin.the-ordinary-squalane-cleanser: A gentle, unscented balm cleanser that reviewers found hydrating and useful as a first cleanse. The catch: it can leave a film and miss eye makeup, so a second cleanse is often needed.
skin.the-ordinary-uv-filters-spf-45-serum: A light, milky chemical sunscreen serum with no white cast, best for normal to dry skin. The catch: the dewy finish turns shiny on oily skin and it is not water resistant.
skin.the-ordinary-vitamin-c-suspension-23-ha-: A strong, waterless vitamin C suspension that gave reviewers brighter skin and lighter pigmentation, if skin tolerates it. The catch: it is gritty, greasy and slow to absorb, and it tingles at first.
skin.torriden-dive-in-low-molecular-hyaluroni: A light, watery low molecular hyaluronic acid serum that hydrates without stickiness and layers well under moisturizer, makeup and sunscreen. The catch: hydration only, so dry skin needs a cream on top.
skin.torriden-dive-in-soothing-cream: A light, cooling gel cream that sinks in fast without stickiness, best for oily, combination or dehydrated skin and hot weather. The catch: the hydration is moderate, so very dry skin needs a richer cream.
skin.torriden-solid-in-ceramide-cream: A thick, buttery ceramide cream that hydrates well for dry, sensitive skin, best at night or in cool weather. The catch: it feels heavy and turns oily or tacky on oily skin or in humidity.
skin.vanicream-daily-facial-moisturizer: A light, fragrance-free lotion with ceramides, hyaluronic acid and squalane that hydrates without greasiness and sits well under makeup. The catch: too light alone for dry skin, and a few reviewers felt a tingle.
skin.vanicream-facial-moisturizer-with-sunscr: A fragrance-free, ceramide mineral moisturizer with SPF 30 that is gentle and hydrating, best for dry or sensitive skin. The catch: white cast at first and a thick, shiny finish.
skin.vanicream-gentle-facial-cleanser: A simple, fragrance-free gel cleanser that cleans gently without stripping, for sensitive or dry skin, often as a second cleanse. The catch: on its own it only partly removes makeup and sunscreen.
skin.vanicream-moisturizing-cream: A thick, petrolatum-based cream that seals in moisture for very dry, itchy skin, best at night and in winter. The catch: it is very heavy for the face in the daytime.
